requestSummary: Design and then implement a new Dockerized LangGraph orchestration project named jessy-graph at /root/hzx_mixlinker/jessy-graph. The host Codex client will use a loopback-only Streamable HTTP MCP service; the container will run the MCP server, LangGraph runtime, Codex CLI workers, Git, and verification tooling.
approvedInScope: Keep jessy-skills as the policy, prompt, role, and versioned task-contract layer
Accept a main-session-approved project task DAG through MCP
Use a ProjectGraph and reusable TaskExecutionSubgraph
Persist runtime entities and LangGraph checkpoints in separate SQLite databases
Run a self-contained Docker image with loopback-only Streamable HTTP MCP exposure
Provision a container-specific CODEX_HOME with relay-specific config.toml and auth.json without mounting the host /root/.codex
Run up to five conflict-free Codex workers with serial integration
Support built-in Go, Python, and Node.js verification command policies
Produce immutable diff, event, log, test, and patch artifacts
approvedOutOfScope: Authentication identities, tenants, or distributed scheduling
Automatic merge, push, pull request creation, deployment, migration, or production changes
Letting jessy-graph redesign or expand the submitted task DAG
Arbitrary shell strings, pipelines, or redirection in verification commands
sourceEvidence: User required LangGraph and the new /root/hzx_mixlinker/jessy-graph project
User selected direct MCP rather than a user-facing CLI
User required the final V1 form to be a Docker image/container connected to host Codex through MCP
User accepted SQLite dual stores, a dedicated integration worktree, M1/M2 delivery, built-in language policies, bounded retries, and main-session-owned planning
User set the global Codex worker concurrency limit to five
constraints: The host source repository must not be modified by jessy-graph
LangGraph checkpoints are recovery data, not the canonical application query model
Git and deterministic validators are evidence authorities; Codex self-reports are not
Every external side effect is idempotent or reconciled before replay
MCP binds to the container network internally but Docker publishes it only on host 127.0.0.1
No Docker socket is mounted into the container
Codex auth.json is supplied from a Docker secret with mode 0600 and never committed or included in image layers
The container-specific config.toml must load the custom Responses provider, so worker execution must not use --ignore-user-config
Container startup must verify the configured relay is reachable and must not silently fall back to direct OpenAI routing
High-pressure whole-repository verification commands remain serial
